input: Set up a cloud backup for all home documents

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: "All home documents" is vague — knowing whether this means only text files, or also photos, videos, financial records, and system files determines storage size and which folders to include.
Whether this backup is for one person or shared across multiple household members changes how accounts, permissions, and folder structures need to be set up.
The operating system and devices in use (Windows, Mac, mobile) directly determine which backup tools and methods are compatible.
Budget determines whether a free-tier service suffices or whether a paid plan with more storage and features is needed.
Some users want a specific provider (Google Drive, iCloud, Backblaze, OneDrive, etc.) based on existing accounts or privacy preferences, which shapes the entire setup path.
Knowing whether backups should run continuously, on a schedule, or manually affects which tool features to configure and how much bandwidth is acceptable.
Whether the goal is simply having a copy in the cloud, or also being able to restore previous versions of files, determines how robust the solution needs to be.

gold.taskTitle: Set up cloud backup for home documents
gold.taskDescription: Configure a reliable cloud backup system to automatically protect all important home documents from a personal device or home network.

questions.title: Which file types should be included in the backup?
questions.description: Determine if the backup covers only documents (PDFs, Word files, spreadsheets) or also photos, videos, financial records, and other file types.

questions.title: Is this backup for one person or the whole household?
questions.description: Clarify whether a single user account is sufficient or if multiple household members need their files backed up under shared or separate accounts.

questions.title: What device and operating system are the files stored on?
questions.description: Identify the primary device (Windows PC, Mac, Linux, mobile) to ensure the chosen backup solution is fully compatible.

questions.title: What is your monthly or annual budget for this backup?
questions.description: Establish whether free-tier cloud storage is acceptable or if a paid plan is on the table, which filters the suitable service options.

questions.title: Do you already use or prefer a specific cloud provider?
questions.description: Find out if the user has an existing preference or account with a service like Google Drive, OneDrive, iCloud, or Backblaze to avoid unnecessary new sign-ups.

questions.title: How often should the backup run automatically?
questions.description: Decide whether backups should be continuous and real-time, scheduled daily or weekly, or triggered manually by the user.

questions.title: Do you need to restore older versions of files, or just the latest copy?
questions.description: Determine if version history is required so accidentally overwritten or deleted files can be recovered, which affects which services and plans are suitable.
